Quick answers while we prepare a short deliverable pack (we'll attach a sample manifest + small data sample):
- Scope: exports can include API request logs, auth/sign-in events, admin console actions, model invocation traces, and telemetry (configurable per-customer).
- Formats: NDJSON or Parquet for bulk consumption; CSV exports for selected fields.
- Preservation: we provide chain-of-custody manifests with SHA-256 hashes for each file and a top-level signed manifest.
- Standard turnaround: will confirm with ops, but expect 5-7 business days for a routine multi-month export. Expedited options are available under enterprise / Dedicated contracts.

Subject: Re: RFP Q4 - Clarify audit log assembly & sampling requests

Hi Katrina —

Following up with the technical playbook we discussed. Below is a concise description you can paste into the RFP response; attaching a tiny sample manifest and a small NDJSON extract for reviewer ingestion.

1) Export assembly (what we include)
- Event classes: api_requests, auth_events, admin_actions, model_invocations, system_telemetry. Each event contains timestamps (ISO8601), actor id, resource id, action, outcome, request_id, and optional payload.
- Per-customer scoping: exports are filtered by customer_id at export time; multi-tenant indices are not exposed.

2) Retention windows & preservation modes
- Default retention: 90 days for high-volume telemetry; 1 year for security-sensitive audit events (auth/admin); configurable up to customer-specified retention periods under Dedicated/Private plans.
- Legal hold: when a hold is requested, we snapshot and preserve matching events in immutable storage until the hold is released. Holds are additive to retention windows.

3) Sampling methodology for auditor review
- Representative sample approach: we provide two artifacts for audit sampling —
  a) Deterministic stratified sample: we compute a SHA-256 seeded pseudo-random sample stratified by event type and time window (seed recorded in manifest).
  b) Statistical random sample: customer-defined percentage (typical: 1%–5%), with sampling anchored to request_id to preserve event families.
- Samples include the manifest lines that specify sampling seed, algorithm, and population size so auditors can reproduce selection.

4) Chain-of-custody & verification
- Each exported file is compressed (.gz) and accompanied by SHA-256 file hashes.
- A top-level manifest (JSON Lines) contains file paths, byte-size, SHA-256, record counts, sampling seed, and UTC timestamps.
- The manifest is signed with Redwood's export-signing key (RSA-4096) and we provide the public key / thumbprint for verification. For Dedicated/Private customers we can sign with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) upon request.

5) Export formats and delivery
- Formats: NDJSON (recommended for audit), Parquet (columnar analytics), CSV for small field extracts.
- Delivery: secure S3 pre-signed links (default), SFTP, or transfer into customer VPC (private lane).

6) Turnaround & SLA (standard vs. expedited)
- Standard (hosted customers): up to 5 business days for exports covering <= 3 months; up to 10 business days for exports 3–12 months.
- Expedited (enterprise / Dedicated customers): 48–72 hours for exports up to 6 months; negotiated terms for larger ranges.
- For legal/eDiscovery holds we offer preservation confirmations within 24 hours and packaged delivery timelines as above.

7) Evidence & audit mapping
- We supply a mapping table to SOC 2 control objectives (available in our confluence export playbook).

Attachments included: sample_export_manifest.ndjson (tiny), sample_events_extract.ndjson (200KB).

If you confirm the exact time range (e.g., 6 months ending 2026-10-31) and whether you need PII redaction, we'll provide the concrete timeline and a formal RFP blurb you can include verbatim.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

Katrina —

Confirmed commitments for the RFP scenario you outlined (you can copy/paste the block below into your RFP response):

Redwood Inference — Formal export & preservation statement (RFP language)
- Scope: Full export of audit logs covering api_requests, auth_events, admin_actions, model_invocations, and telemetry for the specified 6-month period.
- Delivery formats: NDJSON (preferred) and Parquet; gzip-compressed files.
- Chain-of-custody: Each file accompanied by SHA-256 and top-level signed manifest. Redwood can sign manifests with the customer's KMS/HSM key when provided; otherwise Redwood will sign with an RSA-4096 export key and provide the public key/thumbprint.
- Delivery methods: secure S3 pre-signed links, SFTP, or direct transfer into customer VPC.
- SLA: Standard hosted customers — delivery within 7 business days for a 6-month export. Expedited enterprise/Dedicated customers — delivery within 72 business hours for a 6-month export.
- Preservation: On legal hold, data snapshots are preserved in immutable storage until a documented release is received. Redwood provides a preservation confirmation within 24 hours of hold activation and periodic snapshots as requested.
- Expected size (ballpark): for a medium finance customer ingesting ~200 QPS of audit events, expect ~60–150GB per month of raw events (NDJSON gzipped) depending on payload size; we will provide a precise estimate if you share QPS or sample rates.

Next steps: we will attach an RFP-ready one-pager and the signed-manifest example. Please advise if Kestrel intends to provide a KMS key (preferred) or require Redwood-signed manifests.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through the chain-of-custody sample.

-David
David Kim
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
